name: Black Death reaches England
summary: Plague is reported at Melcombe Regis (Weymouth) in June 1348 and reaches London by autumn. Mortality varies sharply by community: rural manors record 40–60% deaths; Westminster Abbey loses 27 of its 50 monks. Repeated waves continue (1361, 1369, 1375).

_quarry.structural_significance: Triggers the legislative response of the Ordinance of Labourers (1349) and Statute of Labourers (1351), attempting (unsuccessfully) to peg wages at pre-plague levels. The accumulated grievance helps drive the 1381 Peasants' Revolt.
